title: Data model for environmental indicators produced by GRETA
description: Represents the environmental indicators calculated by GRETA using Environmental Footprint 3.1 methodology

id.description: Property. Unique identifier for the entity

type.description: Property. NGSI Entity type. Type of message published

acidificationAccumulatedExceedanceAE.description: Property. Acidification refers to the process where emissions of sulfur dioxide (SO₂), nitrogen oxides (NOₓ), and ammonia (NH₃) lead to the formation of acidic compounds in the atmosphere, which then deposit in soils and water bodies, reducing pH levels. This indicator measures the potential impact of these emissions on ecosystems, using an accumulated exceedance approach to assess how much ecosystems can tolerate before damage occurs.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for acidificationAccumulatedExceedanceAE

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

climateChangeGlobalWarmingPotentialGWP.description: Property. This indicator measures the contribution of greenhouse gas emissions to global warming over a 100-year timeframe, expressed in kilograms of CO₂-equivalent. It accounts for all major greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄), and nitrous oxide (N₂O), each normalized to its global warming potential.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for climateChangeGlobalWarmingPotentialGWP

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

climateChangeBiogenicGWP100.description: Property. This measures the global warming potential of biogenic (plant-derived) carbon emissions over a 100-year period, which includes CO₂ released from the combustion or decomposition of biomass. Biogenic emissions are distinguished from fossil emissions, with a focus on the carbon cycle of living organisms.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for climateChangeBiogenicGWP100

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

climateChangeFossilGWP100.description: Property. This indicator measures the global warming potential from fossil fuel-derived emissions, such as CO₂ from coal, oil, and natural gas combustion. It captures the long-term impact of these emissions on climate change, expressed in kilograms of CO₂-equivalents over a 100-year period.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for climateChangeFossilGWP100

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

climateChangeLandUseAndLULUCGWP.description: Property. Land use and land use change (LULUC) impacts on climate change refer to greenhouse gas emissions caused by deforestation, land conversion for agriculture, and other changes in land use. This indicator measures the potential warming effect of land use-related CO₂ emissions over 100 years.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for climateChangeLandUseAndLULUCGWP

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

ecotoxicityFreshwaterComparativeToxicCTU.description: Property. This indicator measures the potential harm of chemical substances released into freshwater ecosystems. It quantifies the toxicity of substances (e.g., heavy metals, pesticides) to aquatic organisms, expressed in Comparative Toxic Units for ecosystems (CTUe). It evaluates the impact on biodiversity and ecosystem health.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for ecotoxicityFreshwaterComparativeToxicCTU

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

ecotoxicityFreshwaterInorganicsCTUe.description: Property. This indicator focuses on the toxicity of inorganic chemical pollutants, such as heavy metals and minerals, in freshwater ecosystems. It assesses the potential for harm to aquatic life due to exposure to these inorganic substances, expressed in CTUe.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for ecotoxicityFreshwaterInorganicsCTUe

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

ecotoxicityFreshwaterOrganicsCTUe.description: Property. This measures the toxicity of organic pollutants, including pesticides, herbicides, and other organic chemicals, in freshwater environments. These pollutants may disrupt aquatic ecosystems and harm species, with impacts measured in Comparative Toxic Units for ecosystems (CTUe).

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for ecotoxicityFreshwaterOrganicsCTUe

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

energyResourcesAbioticDepletionFossils.description: Property. This indicator measures the depletion of non-renewable energy resources, primarily fossil fuels (oil, coal, natural gas). It reflects the consumption of these resources and the impact on their long-term availability, expressed in megajoules (MJ), focusing on energy content and environmental sustainability.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for energyResourcesAbioticDepletionFossils

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

eutrophicationFreshwaterNutrientsP.description: Property. Freshwater eutrophication occurs when excessive nutrients, especially phosphorus (P), enter water bodies, leading to algal blooms and oxygen depletion. This indicator measures the potential for nutrient pollution to cause eutrophication, expressed in kilograms of phosphorus equivalents (kg P-Eq).

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for eutrophicationFreshwaterNutrientsP

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

eutrophicationMarineNutrientsN.description: Property. Marine eutrophication is caused by nitrogen (N) pollution, which can lead to harmful algal blooms in oceans and coastal waters. This indicator measures the impact of nitrogen runoff on marine ecosystems, expressed in kilograms of nitrogen equivalents (kg N-Eq).

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for eutrophicationMarineNutrientsN

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

eutrophicationTerrestrialAccumExceedance.description: Property. This measures the impact of nutrient pollution, particularly nitrogen, on terrestrial ecosystems. It assesses the potential for nutrient accumulation to exceed the natural capacity of the land, leading to changes in vegetation and soil degradation, expressed in mol N-Eq.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for eutrophicationTerrestrialAccumExceedance

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

humanToxicityCarcinogenicCTUh.description: Property. This indicator assesses the potential impact of exposure to carcinogenic substances on human health. It is expressed in Comparative Toxic Units for humans (CTUh) and measures the risk of developing cancer from exposure to various chemicals, such as heavy metals, industrial solvents, and certain organic compounds.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for humanToxicityCarcinogenicCTUh

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

humanToxicityCarcinogenicInorganicsCTU.description: Property. This focuses on the carcinogenic risks to humans from exposure to inorganic substances, such as arsenic, lead, and other heavy metals. It evaluates the potential harm in terms of cancer development, expressed in CTUh.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for humanToxicityCarcinogenicInorganicsCTU

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

humanToxicityCarcinogenicOrganicsCTU.description: Property. This indicator assesses the carcinogenic potential of organic chemical substances, such as formaldehyde, benzene, and pesticides, on human health. It evaluates the risk of cancer associated with exposure to these compounds, expressed in CTUh.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for humanToxicityCarcinogenicOrganicsCTU

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

humanToxicityNonCarcinogenicCTUh.description: Property. This indicator measures the potential risk to human health from non-carcinogenic substances. It assesses the likelihood of harm such as organ damage or neurological effects from exposure to chemicals, expressed in CTUh.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for humanToxicityNonCarcinogenicCTUh

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

humanToxicityNonCarcinogenicInorganicsCT.description: Property. This focuses on non-carcinogenic health risks from inorganic substances, including heavy metals like cadmium and lead. It evaluates the impact of these chemicals on human health, expressed in CTUh.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for humanToxicityNonCarcinogenicInorganicsCTU

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

humanToxicityNonCarcinogenicOrganicsCTU.description: Property. This indicator assesses the non-carcinogenic health risks posed by organic substances, including solvents, pesticides, and other chemicals. It measures the potential for organ damage or other chronic effects, expressed in CTUh.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for humanToxicityNonCarcinogenicOrganicsCTU

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

ionisingRadiationHumanHealthU235.description: Property. This measures the potential health impact of ionizing radiation exposure on humans. It is based on the efficiency of radiation exposure relative to uranium-235 (U235), expressed in kilobecquerels (kBq). This indicator focuses on risks such as radiation sickness or long-term health effects like cancer.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for ionisingRadiationHumanHealthU235

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

landUseSoilQualityIndex.description: Property. This indicator evaluates the impact of land use on soil quality, taking into account factors such as organic carbon content, nutrient availability, and erosion potential. It provides a measure of how land use practices affect soil health and sustainability.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for landUseSoilQualityIndex

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

materialResourcesAbioticDepletionElement.description: Property. This indicator measures the depletion of non-renewable material resources, particularly metals and minerals (e.g., copper, zinc, antimony). It reflects the long-term availability of these elements and the environmental impact of their extraction, expressed in kilograms of antimony equivalents (kg Sb-Eq).

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for materialResourcesAbioticDepletionElements

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

ozoneDepletionPotentialODP.description: Property. This indicator measures the potential for chemical substances to deplete the stratospheric ozone layer. It is expressed in kilograms of CFC-11 equivalents (kg CFC-11-Eq), focusing on substances like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) that contribute to ozone layer depletion.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for ozoneDepletionPotentialODP

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

particulateMatterFormationHealth.description: Property. This indicator assesses the impact of particulate matter (PM) emissions on human health. Particulates such as PM10 and PM2.5 can penetrate the respiratory system, causing conditions like asthma, bronchitis, and cardiovascular diseases. This is expressed in disease incidence cases.

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for particulateMatterFormationHealth

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

photochemicalOxidantFormationHealth.description: Property. This measures the impact of emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and nitrogen oxides (NOx) that lead to the formation of ground-level ozone (smog), which affects human respiratory health. It is expressed in kilograms of NMVOC equivalents (kg NMVOC-Eq).

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for photochemicalOxidantFormationHealth

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed

waterUseUserDeprivationPotential.description: Property. This indicator evaluates the potential for water consumption to lead to human water deprivation, considering local water scarcity and water use efficiency. It is expressed in cubic meters of world equivalents deprived (m³ world Eq. deprived).

unitCode.description: Property. Unit of measurement for waterUseUserDeprivationPotential

observedAt.description: Property. Timestamp when the value was observed
